New since this morning: with Schuurs, Sandler and Nuytinck all out and Fonville doubtful, NEC's makeshift defence is likely to let PSV get more clean shots away than the numbers think, so a mild +3% to about 11.3.

401875544.overall: Struggling Utrecht (14th, 12 pts) host promoted Cambuur (10th, 15 pts), who started with four defeats, then went seven unbeaten before a 5-2 home loss to PSV before the international break; their only away defeat this season came at Fortuna Sittard. Utrecht have lost to Telstar and NEC, have conceded 34 league goals, and coach Anthony Correia is under heavy pressure, with fan banners at the training ground and stadium; he says the team must fix the spacing between the lines rather than change everything. RTV Utrecht confirms Jensen, Engwanda, Paredes, Jonathans and Ohio are still unavailable (Jensen, Engwanda and Paredes trained with the group this week), as the numbers already assume; Cambuur's main threat is Utrecht loanee Rafik El Arguioui (six goals, three assists), and earlier reports had keeper Jasper Meijster out long-term. Referee Allard Lindhout (3.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already counting Cambuur's scoring run (16 in six) and Utrecht's leaky defence (15 conceded in six). Correia himself points to poor spacing in the goals conceded against NEC, Cambuur have El Arguioui in form, and their first-choice keeper Meijster has been reported out, which the numbers give no goal effect; a mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, most of them Utrecht's (6.4). A Utrecht side under pressure at home should push forward and Correia calls Cambuur a team of fighters who sit in and counter, but that is already the shape of the numbers, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for Utrecht's 12 cards in their last six (+10%) and for referee Lindhout's slightly high rate. Fan anger at Utrecht and a scrappy Cambuur side could add some edge, but no suspensions or rivalry point to more, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, with Utrecht expected to take 17.5. Attackers Jonathans, Ohio, Paredes and Jensen are all still out, as the numbers assume, and those absences have lasted for weeks so they are already in Utrecht's recent shot counts; I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already trimming Utrecht for weaker recent accuracy (-6%) and lifting Cambuur (+8%) on El Arguioui's good run. Today's team news confirms what the numbers expected on both sides, so I stay at 10.4.

401875543.overall: Second-placed Feyenoord (25 pts, one behind PSV) host Excelsior (15th, 11 pts), who have lost five league games in a row and failed to score in their last four, including a 9-0 defeat at Twente. Feyenoord are winless in five in all competitions after a 5-3 loss at Heerenveen, and Giovanni van Bronckhorst needs a response. St. Juste (shin, counted) is out until around the winter break, Nieuwkoop, Bos, Beelen and Wessels are out, Smal is back in group training and Moder is being eased back, while Anis Hadj Moussa (ankle, back early from Algeria) only trained partly on Friday and the coach doubts he is fit; Nelson and Van Persie are available again. Excelsior's Nesto Groen is suspended (counted) and Feyenoord loanee Aymen Sliti expects to play despite a thumb knock. The numbers add a big derby boost for cards, but this Rotterdam derby is one-sided and friendly between the clubs (two Feyenoord loanees play for Excelsior), so I trim that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already counting Excelsior's collapse (22 conceded in six), St. Juste's absence and Groen's ban. Feyenoord have Nelson and Van Persie back and a patched defence that has conceded in five straight games, but Excelsior have not scored in four league games, so I lean only slightly higher, to about 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them (6.8) and Excelsior's drop in corners already in the momentum adjustment. Hadj Moussa, Feyenoord's most direct winger, is doubtful, but Van Persie, Valente and Nelson give other wide options, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, and that already includes a +39% derby boost plus referee Robin Hensgens' average record. This city derby is not a hostile one: the clubs work together on loans (Sliti, Plug), Excelsior have not won at De Kuip in decades, and a game with Feyenoord on the ball usually brings few home fouls. I trim it -6% to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 19.2 and Excelsior on just 9.1 after a dismal run (45 shots in six, already counted). Feyenoord's returning attackers support a high home total, but that is already the numbers' expectation, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots and barely hitting the target themselves (9 in six). Sliti should play and Groen is banned, so Excelsior's threat stays small, as the numbers already assume; I stay at 10.9.

401875546.overall: The Derby of the North: Groningen (9th, one point from their last four league games and beaten 2-0 by FC Emmen in the cup) host in-form Heerenveen (6th), who have won four in a row, the last a 5-3 comeback against Feyenoord. Coach Dick Lukkien misses the game after a hip replacement, so assistant Casper Goedkoop leads Groningen from the touchline. Keeper Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer are banned after red cards at AZ and second keeper Rijk Janse is out, so third-choice Lovro Stubljar is expected in goal; Jeng and Hernes are out, but David van der Werff and Wouter Prins return (RTV Noord's expected line-up). Heerenveen's only absence is Hristiyan Petrov, who came back injured from Bulgaria duty (Omrop Fryslan). The bans, the derby boost and referee Alex Bos' slightly above-average card rate are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, already counting both sides' scoring runs (17 goals each in their last six), Vaessen's ban (+6% for Heerenveen) and Hateboer's absence. What they can't see is that Groningen go in with their third-choice keeper because Janse is also out, behind a defence pundits such as Gerald Sibon call the weak spot, and with no head coach on the bench; a mild +3% to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with Groningen's recent drop in corners (22 in six) already counted. Groningen are expected to press high from the first minute and Heerenveen to play through it and counter, which fits the numbers' fairly even split, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a large derby boost (+39%) and Alex Bos' 3.3 cards a game. The rivalry is real (Heerenveen watchers warn 'you feel the hatred' at the Euroborg), but that is exactly what the derby boost covers, and both sides have been light on cards lately, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Heerenveen's sharp recent shooting (+8%) counted. Groningen's high press leaves space behind for a quick side like Heerenveen, but that open style is what the numbers have measured all season, and Van der Werff's return only restores Groningen's usual side, so I stay at 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, with Heerenveen's recent accuracy (+7%) and Groningen's dip (-7%) already in. Stubljar in goal affects how many shots go in rather than how many are on target, and Petrov's absence is a small loss for Heerenveen, so I stay at 10.0.

401875539.overall: A relegation-zone game: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts), both within a few points of the drop. Telstar ended a ten-game winless run with a 4-2 win over Utrecht and drew 2-2 at Fortuna; coach Henk Brugge, who spent twelve years at PEC, has bought time, and NH Nieuws (19 Nov) reports Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes fit again, while Jelani Seedorf is doubtful after an injury in a friendly. PEC are unbeaten in four and this is Alex Pastoor's first league game since he took over on 9 November; they miss Krastev, Rahajaan and now midfielder Gilles van der Wal, with full-back Floranus 50/50. The numbers still count Alders and Mendes as out; referee Joey Kooij's 3.4 cards a game is already in.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and defender Alders out (+6% for PEC). NH Nieuws says both are fit, which would add a little to Telstar's attack and take a little off PEC's, about -1% net, while PEC lose Van der Wal and Telstar may miss Seedorf; these small changes cancel, and both sides concede plenty (counted), so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (25 in six) already counted. Pastoor has said the squad needs little changing, and Telstar's wing play through Martha and Brouwer is what they have shown all season, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's slightly busier recent card count. It is a tense six-pointer near the bottom, but that is normal at this end of the table and no bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu's four goals in six. Mendes returning adds an option but not a big change in volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. A new coach's first league game can be cautious, but Pastoor is keeping the side that went four unbeaten, so I see no reason to move and stay at 10.6.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, two behind PSV, best defence in the league) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, a league-high 40 goals conceded and a league-low 11 scored, and are close to equalling a 42-year-old Eredivisie record for winless games. Jurgen Streppel, back for a second spell since October, says his side will try to play out of Twente's press rather than just hit long balls, while staying compact. Willem II miss captain Justin Hoogma and Amine Lachkar (counted), and keeper Thomas Didillon is doubtful, with Delanghe expected to start. Coach John van den Brom confirmed Unnerstall, Bruns and Thorvaldsen are out (the numbers count only Bruns, but Thorvaldsen has missed five games already, so recent form reflects it); Lemkin is back in training. Referee Serdar Gozubuyuk's high card rate is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six and Willem II's 21 conceded. Thorvaldsen is out for a sixth game, but Twente scored freely without him, and Willem II probably lose first-choice keeper Didillon, which pulls the other way, so I stay at 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, already up for Twente's 46 corners in six (+6%) and down for Willem II's low output. Streppel expects to be pushed back, which is exactly the one-sided pattern those figures describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with Serdar Gozubuyuk's 3.9 a game (+37%) and Willem II's 12 cards in six already counted. A side defending deep for long spells picks up cards, but that is priced in and no suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.6 shots, already lifted strongly for Twente's 145 shots in six (+25%) and cut for Willem II's low output. Streppel wants to keep the ball more, but against the league's best defence that is unlikely to change volumes much, so I stay at 35.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already up for Twente's accuracy (+14%) and down for Willem II's (-9%). Twente's absences are ones they have played without for weeks, so I stay at 11.2.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax (25 pts) host ADO Den Haag (17th, 9 pts), who sacked Robin Peter, won 3-1 against Sparta under interim Levi Schwiebbe and appointed Maurice Steijn on 13 November; this is Steijn's first game in charge, after a full international break to prepare. The big change for Ajax: coach Michel says Julian Brandt, Steven Berghuis, Thilo Kehrer and Anton Gaaei are fit and available (VI, 20 Nov), although Voetbalprimeur expects Brandt to start on the bench; the numbers still take him off completely (-13%). Dolberg (season), Tsygankov and Adingra remain out. ADO miss Pozo and Reischl (counted), with keeper Nikiema expected to start. Referee Erwin Blank's slightly low card rate is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals with Brandt taken off completely (-13% for Ajax). He is now fit, but likely only for a spell off the bench, so I give back a small part of that cut, partly offset by a new coach in Steijn who will want ADO compact in his first game; about +2% to 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent count and ADO's normal output already counted. Ajax will have most of the ball and Michel wants more pressing energy, which the 6.7 home corners already reflect, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already nudged up for both sides' recent cards and down for Erwin Blank's lighter touch (-5%). No suspensions or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, already up for Ajax's recent volume (+9%) and ADO's (+7%). Brandt and Berghuis back adds options, but a compact ADO under Steijn may also shoot less, so I stay at 34.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target with Brandt ruled out. With him and Berghuis available from the bench and Amrabat and Kehrer back in the side, Ajax have more quality than the numbers assume; a small +2% to about 10.7.

401875540.overall: Sparta (12th, 12 pts) host AZ (5th, 23 pts), who have won only one of their last five league games and travel to Sparta Prague in the Europa League next. AZ coach Leeroy Echteld confirmed on 20 November that Kees Smit, Lewis Schouten and Weslley Patati are not expected back before the winter break, and Jizz Hornkamp (counted) is also set to miss the trip; Valdemar Byskov is back, and Wouter Goes and keeper Owusu-Oduro are 50/50. The numbers count only Hornkamp, Zoet and Resink for AZ, though Smit has been out about six weeks so recent form partly shows it. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO before the break and miss keeper Michael Brouwer, Teo Quintero and Nick Verschuren, with Julian Baas likely back from illness; the numbers list no Sparta absences. Referee Ingmar Oostrom's slightly above-average card rate is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already taking about 5% off AZ for Hornkamp and counting Sparta's 16 conceded in six. AZ's extra absences (Smit, Patati, Schouten) weaken their attack, while Sparta are without keeper Brouwer and defenders Quintero and Verschuren, which helps AZ; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, with AZ's low corners conceded and Sparta's normal output already counted. Losing wide man Patati could cut AZ's crossing a little, but Byskov's return offsets it, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in six (+8%) and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). No suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, with AZ's 93 shots in six counted (+8%). AZ are short of attacking depth with Patati, Schouten and the creative Smit all out on top of Hornkamp, confirmed by Echteld, and a European trip follows, so I trim slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already lifted a little for AZ's accuracy (+6%). With fewer attacking options for AZ than the numbers assume, I shade it to about 9.9.

401875542.overall: Go Ahead Eagles (8th, 17 pts) host Fortuna Sittard (7th, 20 pts), who have drawn five of their last six, most recently 2-2 at home to Telstar. Fortuna are badly hit: forwards Ole Romeny and Lequincio Zeefuik, midfielder Edouard Michut, centre-back Rodrigo Guth and Daley Sinkgraven are out until December or January; the brief lists no Fortuna absences, so the numbers only see them through recent form (about four games). Mohamed Ihattaren (four goals, four assists) carries their attack. Go Ahead won 1-0 at Excelsior last time and beat Groningen in a friendly over the break; Marsman and Saathof are out as the numbers know. Referee Martijn Vos (4.6 cards a game) is already a large part of the cards number; match-specific previews were thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Fortuna are without forwards Romeny and Zeefuik and midfielder Michut, none of whom the numbers take off, and have scored only 8 in their last six (partly counted). Guth's absence weakens their defence a little, which pulls the other way, so I trim to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, already cut a little for Fortuna's low recent count (20 in six). Go Ahead should press and push down the wings as usual at De Adelaarshorst, and Fortuna's absences are already showing in that low count, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards: Martijn Vos's very high card rate (+40%) pushes it up, while Go Ahead's 4 cards in their last six and Fortuna's low count pull it down, all already counted. No bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Fortuna's shooting is down recently (64 in six, counted) and they are still missing several first-choice attackers the numbers don't list, so I lean lower to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With Romeny, Zeefuik and Michut out and Ihattaren left to carry the attack, Fortuna should test Go Ahead's keeper less than the numbers assume; about 9.3.

401875001.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 points, one win in five) host second-placed Inter (28 points, four wins in five), with Sarri's side well short of last season's level and Chivu's Inter chasing the top spot. Atalanta's defence is in trouble: Hien and Kossounou are out and Kristensen is struggling to recover, so Kolasinac moves into the middle, while Kessie only returned from international duty on Friday; none of this is in the numbers, which list no Atalanta absences. Inter start Thuram with Pio Esposito, with Lautaro back from injury for the bench; Bonny and Stankovic are out (only Stankovic counted). Referee Fabio Maresca (4.8 cards a game) and a lively head-to-head are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. With Kristensen now also struggling, Atalanta could be without three centre-backs, which the numbers don't know, against an Inter attack with Thuram starting and Lautaro to come on; a mild lean up to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already raised for Inter's recent corner count against an Atalanta side conceding many. Nothing in the team news changes the wide play of either side, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and already add Maresca's high rate (+26%) and a lively head-to-head (+13%). No suspension threat or new rivalry angle has been reported, so I stay at about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already lifted for Inter's shooting. Atalanta's makeshift back line points up for Inter, while Atalanta, short of rhythm in midfield with Kessie back late, may create a bit less, so nothing clear moves it; about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Inter's forwards should find clearer chances against a back line built around Kolasinac in the middle and without Hien, Kossounou and probably Kristensen; a small nudge to about 9.6.

401876400.overall: Marseille (4th, 18 points) have won five league games in a row under Bruno Genesio and have scored 22, while promoted Le Mans (15th, 8 points) are winless in five and have conceded in every league game. Genesio says all his internationals are back and only Emerson and Cornelius are out, both counted; he calls Le Mans very organised with two forwards who run in behind, and expects Marseille to have most of the ball. Le Mans miss Bourabaa and Sidibé (counted); the latest probable lineups have captain Yohou starting and list no other doubts, so they look less depleted than reported earlier in the week. Marseille host Levski Sofia in the Europa League on Thursday, and referee Eric Wattellier (3.5 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take a large share off Le Mans for Bourabaa. Marseille are in form and nearly at full strength, while Genesio warns about Le Mans' counters and a European game on Thursday may mean some game management once Marseille lead; these balance out, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. Le Mans' back five and Marseille's narrow attacking midfield (Harit, Abdelli) are already in the numbers, so I stay at 8.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already take some off for Wattellier's lenient record. With no rivalry here and nothing pointing to a heated game, I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. This morning I nudged it up because Le Mans had several doubts, but the latest news has Yohou and the others fit, so Le Mans should be at the strength the numbers expect; I go back to 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Marseille's attack is unchanged and scoring every week, which the numbers already show, so I stay at 9.3.

401882803.overall: Getafe (15th, 12 pts) host Atlético Madrid (3rd, 28 pts) on Sunday night; Bordalás's Getafe are unbeaten at home this season (three wins, three draws), while Atlético come off defeats to Bayern and Barcelona but have won four straight away games, and Simeone has won eight of his last ten visits to Getafe. Gudelj is banned and Uche and Juanmi are out (in the numbers); Zaid Romero is a doubt and Mayoral is over a stomach bug. Atlético are without Lookman and Pubill (in the numbers), and Cuti Romero is also ruled out, which the numbers don't list but which is already in their recent results after five missed games; Julián Álvarez, Sørloth, Giuliano Simeone and Hjulmand were still finishing recovery work after international duty. Atlético host Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. No referee had been named in the pages I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and take Lookman and Pubill off. What they can't see: several Atlético internationals were still doing recovery work on Thursday, and Getafe's home games under Bordalás are slow and tight, with previews expecting a set-piece game. A small lean down to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already count Getafe's high recent corner count (38 in six games). Getafe play direct and win corners from long balls and crosses at home, while Atlético have less pace out wide without Lookman, which the numbers count. Nothing points clearly either way, so 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, counting both teams' card form and past meetings, but the game is not flagged as a derby. It is a Madrid-area meeting against a Bordalás side built on fouls, duels and slowing the game, and these meetings tend to get heated. With no referee named yet, a mild lean up to about 5.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots, and recent form has already pushed both sides up (+13% Getafe, +8% Atlético). Getafe rely on long balls and rarely build many shots, and Atlético's tired internationals point to a managed game; the Champions League game is Wednesday against Viking, so heavy rotation is less likely than I first thought. A small trim to about 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. A slow, stop-start game with Atlético's forwards just back from international duty should mean few clear chances, while Lookman's absence is already counted. A slight lean down to about 7.2.

401883111.overall: Sixth-placed Burgos (24 points, 17 of them from eight home games) host 19th-placed Albacete (13 points) on Sunday night at El Plantío. Burgos, under Sergio Francisco, lost 3-1 at Leganés last time; they press, attack quickly with full-backs joining and score many from set pieces, but are without forwards Jon Karrikaburu and David González and also Brais Martínez, of whom only González is in the numbers. Albacete have been transformed under Joseba Etxeberria, with four straight league wins (latest 1-0 v Celta Fortuna) and a chance to climb out of the bottom four. They miss Puertas and the suspended José Corpas (last game of his ban) plus several others out for weeks; striker Munir is back in group training after almost three months but may not be ready. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take about 11% off Burgos's goals for David González. Karrikaburu is out too and the numbers don't know it, leaving Álex Forés and Curro Sánchez to carry Burgos against an Albacete side that has kept things tight during its winning run, so I trim a little, to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 5.5 of them Burgos's, already lifted 7% for their recent corner count; they attack wide and live off set pieces and long restarts. Albacete's three-man midfield may keep more of the ball, but that does not clearly change corners, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already adding about 9% for both sides' recent bookings. Burgos's press and Albacete's need for points could mean some duels, but nothing suggests extra needle and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, 17 of them Burgos's after a big 23% boost for their recent shooting. With Karrikaburu and Brais Martínez out beyond what the numbers know, I expect slightly fewer home shots and trim to about 25.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Burgos's missing forwards should mean slightly fewer clear chances, so I trim a little, to about 7.8.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games, eight from safety, and lost 2-0 at Tenerife in Sergio Lobera's first game after José Juan Romero was sacked. Almería, under Xavier García Pimienta, lead with 32 points, are unbeaten in 11 and have the best defence (11 conceded), with Miguel de la Fuente the league's top scorer; a local analyst notes they have struggled to hold leads late in games over the past month. Lobera has had a full week to bring in his possession and pressing ideas; at Tenerife Ceuta had about 64% of the ball but few clear chances. Almería get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty, with only Ely and Melamed out; Ceuta's Edgar Sevikyan went off injured at Tenerife with no update since. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.2 of them Ceuta's, helped by last season's 3-2 home win in the head-to-head. I lean slightly lower, to about 3.1: Ceuta have scored 10 in 14 and under Lobera had the ball at Tenerife but little presence in the box, Sevikyan is a doubt, and Almería have conceded only 11 all season. Almería's own scoring is already in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, which already includes their recent run of winning lots of corners (+11.4% momentum). Lobera's possession style fits that pattern rather than changing it, and Almería tend to let opponents have the ball, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum). Ceuta are desperate and at Tenerife were booked for stopping counters when their press was beaten, which is the same pattern; no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots, with Ceuta's recent shot volume already adding a large 30% to their side. Under Lobera they kept the ball and shot from range, while Almería tend to need few chances; that fits what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I take a little off, to about 10.0: Ceuta managed only two on target at Tenerife despite most of the ball, their shooting is mostly from distance, and Sevikyan may be missing; Almería's own accuracy and their solid defence are already in the numbers.

401875009.overall: A meeting of two struggling sides on Monday night: Monza (Ivan Juric) are 18th with 7 points and have lost four of their last five, while Fiorentina (Paolo Vanoli) are 15th with 9 points after three games unbeaten. Both have scored 17 and conceded 25 in 11 games, so open, leaky games are the norm. Monza rely on Gustavo Varela, the league's top scorer; captain Pessina and Robinson are now fully available, while Folorunsho is still training apart (counted out) and Maye is a doubt.
